title: Rates and Unit Rates
contentObjective: I can find a unit rate to compare prices and decide the better buy.
languageObjective: I can explain my choice using the words rate, unit rate, per, and better buy.

noticeAndWonder.context: Two ticket booths at NeonPlex Arcade post their price signs side by side. Booth A's sign reads "$3 for 5 games." Booth B's sign reads "$5 for 8 games." Players keep arguing about which booth is the better deal just by glancing at the signs.
noticeStarters: I notice Booth A is $___ for ___ games and Booth B is $___ for ___ games.
I notice neither sign gives the price of a single game.
I notice Booth B costs more money but also gives more games.
wonderStarters: I wonder which booth is really the better deal.
I wonder how much ___ games would cost at each booth.
I wonder what I could work out to compare the two signs fairly.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Which Token Pack Is the Better Buy?
revealWordProblem.text: NeonPlex Arcade sells game tokens in two packs. The Starter Pack gives 20 tokens for $5.00. The Mega Pack gives 50 tokens for $11.00. A player wants the lowest cost per token. Which pack is the better buy, and what is the cost per token for each pack?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Starter Pack: $5.00 ÷ 20 = $0.25 per token. Mega Pack: $11.00 ÷ 50 = $0.22 per token. The Mega Pack is the better buy because $0.22 per token is less than $0.25 per token.

turnAndTalk.question: Booth A charges $3 for 5 games and Booth B charges $5 for 8 games. Can you tell which is the better deal just by looking at the signs? Why or why not?
turnAndTalk.kernel: You can't compare fairly until you find the cost per 1 game (the unit rate) for each booth.

turnAndTalk.question: How did you find the cost per game for each booth, and which booth wins?

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute $0.60/game for Booth A and $0.625/game for Booth B, then choose Booth A because the lower unit rate is the better buy.
turnAndTalk.extend: If a player only wants 5 games total, does the better unit rate always give the cheaper total? Explain when it might not.

turnAndTalk.question: At the snack bar, how would you use a unit rate to find the best popcorn deal among different sizes?

stems.en: I would find the price per ___ for each popcorn size.

stems.en: The best deal is the one with the ___ unit rate.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students describe dividing price by size to get a per-unit cost and choosing the lowest unit rate as the best deal.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why might the biggest popcorn not always be the best value? Use the idea of unit rate to explain.

turnAndTalk.kernel: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. The lower cost per item is the better buy.

mission.title: Best Booth in the Arcade
mission.story: You are the new operations manager at NeonPlex Arcade. Two ticket booths are competing for players — Booth A charges $3 for 5 games, Booth B charges $5 for 8 games. Players want the best deal, and your job is to crown the winning booth by mastering unit rates.
mission.objective: Find the cost per game (unit rate) for each booth so you can prove which deal wins.

scenes.name: Booth Showdown

scenes.name: Control Panel
scenes.text: Learn the terms that power the arcade: rate, unit rate, per, and better buy.

scenes.name: Price Calculator
scenes.text: Compute the cost per game for every booth to reveal the best value.

scenes.name: High-Score Run
scenes.text: Clear the rate challenges. The arcade adapts the difficulty to keep you leveling up.

scenes.name: Snack Bar
scenes.text: Use unit rates to find the best popcorn deal at the snack counter.

scenes.name: Final Score
scenes.text: Lock in your verdict and show the arcade you can compare any rate.

finale.title: Top Score Unlocked!
finale.text: You crowned the best booth and the players are lining up. NeonPlex Arcade just made you head of operations — because you can spot the best unit rate every time.

vocabulary.definition: A rate compares different units; a unit rate compares a quantity to 1 unit.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa compara unidades diferentes; una tasa unitaria compara una cantidad con 1 unidad.
vocabulary.visual: 180 miles in 3 hours = 60 miles per 1 hour.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares two quantities with different units is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the cost or amount for one unit is a ___.

examples.why: It gives the amount for exactly one unit.
That is a rate for 3 units, not a unit rate.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Por cada uno. Ejemplo: 5 dólares por libro.
vocabulary.visual: 60 miles per hour means 60 miles for every 1 hour

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: The choice that costs less for each item.

launch.narrative: You're comparing ticket prices at different game booths in the arcade. Booth A charges $3 for 5 games, and Booth B charges $5 for 8 games. Which booth gives you a better deal? To find out, you need to figure out the cost per game — that's the unit rate!

Which booth seems like a better deal at first glance?

conceptIntro.heading: What is a unit rate, and how does it help me find the better buy?
conceptIntro.intro: A rate compares two amounts with different units. A unit rate tells you the amount for just 1 of something, like the cost for 1 game.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. The lower cost per item is the better buy.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Booth A charges $3 for 5 games. I want the cost for just 1 game.
I divide the cost by the games: $3 ÷ 5 = $0.60.
So Booth A costs $0.60 per game. That is the unit rate.
Now I can compare this booth fairly with any other booth.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A booth charges $4 for 8 games. What do we divide?
What is the cost for just 1 game? ($0.50 per game.)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the table, find the cost per game for each booth by dividing.
Then decide which booth has the lowest unit rate — that is the better buy.

explore.instructions: Calculate the unit rate (cost per game) for each arcade booth. Divide the total cost by the number of games.

discourse.prompt: How does finding the unit rate help you compare the booths?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The best deal is Booth ___ because its unit rate of ___ per game is the ___.

approaching.stem: A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: You divided by 10 instead of by 9. Divide the price by the number of games.
Divide the cost by the number of games.
That's the total cost, not the cost per one game.
hints: You know the total cost ($4.50) and the total games (9). A unit rate tells the cost of just ONE game.
To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of games so the second quantity becomes 1.
Set up the division: $4.50 ÷ 9. Think of $4.50 as 450 cents if that makes the division easier.
approaching.stemEs: Un puesto cobra $4.50 por 9 juegos. ¿Cuál es la tasa unitaria?
hintsEs: Conoces el costo total ($4.50) y el total de juegos (9). Una tasa unitaria dice el costo de UN solo juego.
Para hallar una tasa unitaria, divide el costo total entre el número de juegos para que la segunda cantidad sea 1.
Plantea la división: $4.50 ÷ 9. Piensa en $4.50 como 450 centavos si eso te facilita la división.

approaching.stem: A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
choiceFeedback: That's the denominator — divide miles by gallons instead.
That's the numerator — you need to divide miles by gallons.
Not quite. 180 miles ÷ 6 gallons = ___ miles per gallon.
hints: Notice the units in the question: miles PER gallon. That tells you miles go on top and gallons on the bottom.
Divide the total miles by the total gallons so you get the miles for just 1 gallon.
Start the division: 180 ÷ 6. Think: 6 × what number lands on 180?
approaching.stemEs: Un carro recorre 180 millas usando 6 galones de gasolina. ¿Cuál es la tasa unitaria en millas por galón?
hintsEs: Fíjate en las unidades de la pregunta: millas POR galón. Eso te dice que las millas van arriba y los galones abajo.
Divide el total de millas entre el total de galones para obtener las millas de 1 solo galón.
Empieza la división: 180 ÷ 6. Piensa: 6 × ¿qué número da 180?

approaching.stem: A pack of 8 markers costs $6.00. What is the cost per marker?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. $6.00 ÷ 8 = ___ per marker.
Try dividing cost by quantity the correct way.
Not quite. $6.00 ÷ 8 = ___ per marker.
hints: You have 8 markers costing $6.00 total. 'Cost per marker' means the price of ONE marker.
Divide the total price by the number of markers — cost goes first, markers second.
Set up $6.00 ÷ 8. Tip: $6.00 is 600 cents, so try 600 ÷ 8 cents.
approaching.stemEs: Un paquete de 8 marcadores cuesta $6.00. ¿Cuál es el costo por marcador?
hintsEs: Tienes 8 marcadores que cuestan $6.00 en total. 'Costo por marcador' significa el precio de UN marcador.
Divide el precio total entre el número de marcadores: el costo va primero y los marcadores después.
Plantea $6.00 ÷ 8. Consejo: $6.00 son 600 centavos, así que prueba 600 ÷ 8 centavos.

approaching.explanation: A unit rate has 1 in the second quantity. '12 miles per 1 hour' is the only choice where the second quantity is 1.
choiceFeedback: This is a rate, but for 2 hours, not 1 hour.
This is a rate, but for 3 gallons, not 1 gallon.
This is a rate, but for 5 games, not 1 game.
hints: A unit rate always compares to exactly ONE of something — look at the second number in each choice.
Check each choice: is the second quantity (hours, gallons, games) equal to 1? Only one choice passes that test.
Start with '24 miles in 2 hours' — the second quantity is 2, not 1, so that one is not a unit rate. Test the rest the same way.
hintsEs: Una tasa unitaria siempre compara con exactamente UNO de algo; mira el segundo número de cada opción.
Revisa cada opción: ¿la segunda cantidad (horas, galones, juegos) es igual a 1? Solo una opción pasa esa prueba.
Empieza con '24 millas en 2 horas': la segunda cantidad es 2, no 1, así que esa no es tasa unitaria. Prueba las demás igual.

approaching.instructions: Find the unit rate for each arcade deal.
hints: Look at Deal A's finished row: $6.00 for 12 games became $0.50 per game. Your rows work the same way.
For each deal, divide the total cost by the number of games to get the price of one game.
For Deal B, divide $7.50 by 10 games. Then do Deal C: $4.80 ÷ 8.
approaching.instructionsEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de cada oferta del arcade.
hintsEs: Mira la fila terminada de la Oferta A: $6.00 por 12 juegos se volvió $0.50 por juego. Tus filas funcionan igual.
Para cada oferta, divide el costo total entre el número de juegos para obtener el precio de un juego.
Para la Oferta B, divide $7.50 entre 10 juegos. Luego haz la Oferta C: $4.80 ÷ 8.

approaching.title: Spot Diego's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: A booth charges $6.00 for 8 games. Find the unit rate (the cost per game).

workedExample.label: Diego's Attempt
workedExample.work: Diego divided 8 ÷ 6 = 1.33 and wrote the unit rate as $1.33 per game.

workedExample.label: Check
workedExample.work: A single arcade game costing more than a dollar out of a $6.00 booth seems way too high — something is backwards.

approaching.correctWork: To find the cost per game, divide the cost by the number of games: $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per game. Diego divided backwards (games ÷ cost) instead of cost ÷ games.
hints: Which number should be on top when you're finding 'dollars per game' — the dollars or the games?
To find cost per game, divide the cost by the number of games: $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per game.

onLevel.instructions: Complete the table to find unit rates and determine the best deal.
hints: Each pack lists tokens and a total cost. The unit rate column wants the cost of ONE token, like '$0.25 per token'.
Divide the cost by the number of tokens for each pack — dollars ÷ tokens = dollars per token.
For Pack A, divide $5.00 by 20 tokens. Then repeat: $7.00 ÷ 35 for Pack B and $12.50 ÷ 50 for Pack C.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Completa la tabla para encontrar las tasas unitarias y determinar la mejor oferta.
hintsEs: Cada paquete indica fichas y un costo total. La columna de tasa unitaria quiere el costo de UNA ficha, como '$0.25 por ficha'.
Divide el costo entre el número de fichas de cada paquete: dólares ÷ fichas = dólares por ficha.
Para el Paquete A, divide $5.00 entre 20 fichas. Luego repite: $7.00 ÷ 35 para el Paquete B y $12.50 ÷ 50 para el C.

onLevel.stem: Which token pack from the table above is the best deal?
onLevel.explanation: Pack B has a unit rate of $0.20 per token, which is the lowest cost per token.
choiceFeedback: Look at the unit rates for all three packs more carefully.
Find the unit rate for every option (price divided by quantity) and compare them — the best deal is the one with the lowest cost per item.
The unit rates are different; compare them.
hints: The 'best deal' is the pack where ONE token costs the least — not the pack with the most tokens.
Line up the three unit rates you found in the table and look for the smallest cost per token.
Compare $0.25, $0.20, and $0.25 per token. Which of those is the smallest amount of money?

onLevel.instructions: Sort each situation by whether the unit rate is 'per item' or 'per time'.
hints: Look at what comes right after the word 'per' in each card — that word tells you the category.
If 'per' is followed by a time word (hour, minute), it is a per-time rate. If it names a thing (pound, token, bottle), it is per-item.
Try '$3 per pound of apples' first: a pound is a thing, not a time, so it goes in Rate Per Item. Test each card the same way.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada situación según si la tasa unitaria es 'por artículo' o 'por tiempo'.
hintsEs: Mira lo que viene justo después de la palabra 'por' en cada tarjeta: esa palabra te dice la categoría.
Si después de 'por' va una palabra de tiempo (hora, minuto), es una tasa por tiempo. Si nombra una cosa (libra, ficha, botella), es por artículo.
Prueba primero '$3 por libra de manzanas': una libra es una cosa, no un tiempo, así que va en Tasa Por Artículo. Prueba cada tarjeta igual.

onLevel.stem: Runner A completes 4 laps in 12 minutes. Runner B completes 5 laps in 14 minutes. Who runs more laps per minute?
onLevel.explanation: Runner A: 4÷12 ≈ 0.33 laps/min. Runner B: 5÷14 ≈ 0.36 laps/min. Runner B runs slightly more laps per minute.
choiceFeedback: Compute both rates and compare them.
Both cabinets give you enough data to find their rates.
hints: Each runner has laps and minutes. 'More laps per minute' means you need each runner's laps-per-minute rate first.
Divide laps by minutes for BOTH runners, then compare the two decimals — bigger decimal means faster.
Start with Runner A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 laps per minute. Now find Runner B's rate with 5 ÷ 14 and compare.
onLevel.stemEs: El corredor A completa 4 vueltas en 12 minutos. El corredor B completa 5 vueltas en 14 minutos. ¿Quién corre más vueltas por minuto?
hintsEs: Cada corredor tiene vueltas y minutos. 'Más vueltas por minuto' significa que primero necesitas la tasa de vueltas por minuto de cada uno.
Divide vueltas entre minutos para AMBOS corredores y luego compara los dos decimales: mayor decimal significa más rápido.
Empieza con el Corredor A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 vueltas por minuto. Ahora halla la tasa del Corredor B con 5 ÷ 14 y compara.

onLevel.title: Spot Amara's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: Tokens Pack A: 20 tokens for $5.00. Tokens Pack B: 35 tokens for $7.00. Which pack is the better deal?

workedExample.label: Amara's Attempt
workedExample.work: Amara said, 'Pack A is the better deal because it costs less money overall — $5.00 is less than $7.00.'

workedExample.label: Check
workedExample.work: Amara compared the total prices, but the packs have different numbers of tokens, so comparing totals isn't a fair comparison.

onLevel.correctWork: Find the unit rate for each pack: Pack A = $5.00 ÷ 20 = $0.25 per token. Pack B = $7.00 ÷ 35 = $0.20 per token. Since $0.20 is less than $0.25, Pack B is actually the better deal, even though its total price is higher.
hints: Comparing total price only works fairly when both packs have the same number of tokens. Do they?
Divide each pack's cost by its number of tokens to get the unit rate: $5.00 ÷ 20 = $0.25 per token vs. $7.00 ÷ 35 = $0.20 per token.

extending.title: Find the Rate Error

workedExample.label: Find the unit rate: 12 tickets for $8
Write the unit rate
workedExample.work: The unit rate is $1.50 per ticket

extending.correctWork: To find cost per ticket, divide $8 ÷ 12 = $0.67 per ticket (rounded). The student divided tickets by cost instead of cost by tickets.
hints: What should go in the numerator — the cost or the tickets?
To find 'dollars per ticket,' divide dollars by tickets: $8 ÷ 12 ≈ $0.67 per ticket.

extending.prompt: An arcade sells tokens in three packs: 25 tokens for $5, 60 tokens for $10.80, and 100 tokens for $19. A student says the 100-token pack is always the best deal because you get the most tokens. Is the student correct? Find all three unit rates and explain.
extending.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because the best deal is the ___ pack with a unit rate of $___ per token.
extending.hint: Start by finding the unit rate (cost per token) for each pack by dividing the total cost by the number of tokens.
hints: The student only looked at token COUNT. The question asks you to judge the deals by unit rate — cost per token.
Find dollars per token for all three packs by dividing each price by its tokens, then compare the three rates.
First pack: $5 ÷ 25 tokens = $0.20 per token. Now do $10.80 ÷ 60 and $19 ÷ 100, then see which rate is lowest.
extending.promptEs: Un arcade vende fichas en tres paquetes: 25 fichas por $5, 60 fichas por $10.80 y 100 fichas por $19. Un estudiante dice que el paquete de 100 fichas siempre es la mejor oferta porque recibes más fichas. ¿Tiene razón? Encuentra las tres tasas unitarias y explica.
hintsEs: El estudiante solo miró la CANTIDAD de fichas. La pregunta te pide juzgar las ofertas por tasa unitaria: costo por ficha.
Halla los dólares por ficha de los tres paquetes dividiendo cada precio entre sus fichas y luego compara las tres tasas.
Primer paquete: $5 ÷ 25 fichas = $0.20 por ficha. Ahora haz $10.80 ÷ 60 y $19 ÷ 100, y mira cuál tasa es la menor.

extending.instructions: Two water fountains fill bottles at different rates. Fountain A fills 3 bottles in 5 minutes. Fountain B fills 7 bottles in 10 minutes. Compare their rates.
hints: The last column asks for bottles per MINUTE, so bottles get divided by minutes — not the other way around.
Turn each fountain into a decimal rate: bottles ÷ minutes. Then the bigger decimal wins the 'Faster?' row.
For Fountain A, divide 3 by 5 to get its bottles per minute. Then divide 7 by 10 for Fountain B and compare.
extending.instructionsEs: Dos bebederos llenan botellas a tasas diferentes. El bebedero A llena 3 botellas en 5 minutos. El bebedero B llena 7 botellas en 10 minutos. Compara sus tasas.
hintsEs: La última columna pide botellas por MINUTO, así que las botellas se dividen entre los minutos, no al revés.
Convierte cada fuente en una tasa decimal: botellas ÷ minutos. Luego el decimal mayor gana la fila '¿Más rápida?'.
Para la Fuente A, divide 3 entre 5 para obtener sus botellas por minuto. Luego divide 7 entre 10 para la Fuente B y compara.

optionalActivity.name: Arcade Builder Escape Room
optionalActivity.intro: You are locked inside NeonPlex Arcade after hours, and the only way out is to power up each station by cracking its unit-rate code!

optional.stem: Lock 1 — Star Blaster Station: The high-score machine flashes '120 points in 4 minutes'. What is the unit rate in points per minute?
optional.explanation: Divide points by minutes: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 points per minute.
choiceFeedback: You found 90 × 3 — remember, a unit rate comes from dividing, not multiplying.
You picked one of the original numbers. Divide the points by the games to find the rate for one game.
optional.stemEs: Cerradura 1 — Estación Star Blaster: La máquina de puntajes altos muestra '120 puntos en 4 minutos'. ¿Cuál es la tasa unitaria en puntos por minuto?

optional.stem: Pixel Racer: 250 points in 5 min. Turbo Drift: 180 points in 4 min. Which is faster (more points per minute)?
choices: They earn points at the same rate
optional.explanation: Pixel Racer: 250 ÷ 5 = 50 points per minute. Turbo Drift: 180 ÷ 4 = 45 points per minute. 50 > 45, so Pixel Racer is faster.
choiceFeedback: Compute the rate for each game by dividing. One rate is larger — which is faster?
Both numbers are rates, but they're not the same. Divide to compare them carefully.
optional.stemEs: Pixel Racer: 250 puntos en 5 min. Turbo Drift: 180 puntos en 4 min. ¿Cuál es más rápido (más puntos por minuto)?
choicesEs: Ganan puntos a la misma tasa

optional.stem: Lock 3 — Claw Machine Vault: Three coin deals glow on the screen. Which deal is the best value (lowest cost per play)?
optional.explanation: $5.00 ÷ 10 = $0.50 per play; $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per play; $9.00 ÷ 12 = $0.75 per play; $7.00 ÷ 10 = $0.70 per play. The lowest unit rate, $0.50 per play, is the best value.
choiceFeedback: Compute the unit rate (coins per play) for each option. The lowest is the best value.
Two options have different rates. Find both and compare — which costs fewer coins per play?

optional.instructions: Lock 4 — Control Panel: Each arcade machine shows a unit rate. Sort each one by what it measures: points scored per minute, or money paid per play.
optional.instructionsEs: Cerradura 4 — Panel de control: Cada máquina del arcade muestra una tasa unitaria. Clasifica cada una según lo que mide: puntos anotados por minuto o dinero pagado por partida.

optional.label: Lock 5 — Code Cracker: Match each arcade rate to its correct unit rate to unlock the final hallway.
optional.labelEs: Cerradura 5 — Descifra el código: Une cada tasa del arcade con su tasa unitaria correcta para abrir el pasillo final.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Final Exit Lock

workedExample.label: Problem: A coin machine gives 150 coins for $6.00. Find the cost per coin (the unit rate).
Write the unit rate
workedExample.work: The unit rate is $25 per coin

optional.correctWork: To find dollars per coin, divide dollars by coins: $6.00 ÷ 150 = $0.04 per coin. The student divided coins by dollars instead of dollars by coins, which gives coins per dollar, not cost per coin.
hints: Think about what 'cost per coin' means — which quantity should be on top, the dollars or the coins?
To find dollars per coin, divide dollars by coins: $6.00 ÷ 150 = $0.04 per coin. ($25 per coin would be impossible — that is more than the whole machine costs!)

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Rates and Unit Rates is dividing the numbers in the wrong order — for example, finding games ÷ cost instead of cost ÷ games. This flips the rate (games per dollar instead of dollars per game) and gives a number that looks reasonable but answers the wrong question. Another common mistake is comparing the total prices of two deals instead of their unit rates — a bigger total cost does not always mean a worse deal. Before you answer, ask: 'What is 1 unit of, and did I divide the cost by that unit?'

diagram.title: Popcorn Cost Per Cup
diagram.caption: Each bar shows the unit rate ($ per cup) after dividing price by cups; the shorter bar, the large bag at $0.70, is the better buy.

connect.scenario: The arcade snack bar sells popcorn in two sizes: a small bag with 3 cups for $2.25 and a large bag with 8 cups for $5.60. You want the most popcorn for your money.
connect.promptQuestion: Which size is the better deal, and how do you know?
connect.prompt: The ___ bag is the better deal because its unit rate is $___ per cup, which is ___ than $___ per cup for the other size.

check.stem: What is the unit rate for the small bag?
What is the unit rate for the large bag?
Which size is the better deal, and why?
choices: The large bag, because $0.70 per cup is less than $0.75 per cup
The small bag, because $2.25 is less than $5.60
The small bag, because it has fewer cups
check.explanation: The bag with the lower price per cup gives more popcorn for your money, and $0.70 < $0.75. Comparing $2.25 to $5.60 is unfair — the bags hold different amounts.

connect.modelAnswer: Small bag: $2.25 ÷ 3 = $0.75 per cup. Large bag: $5.60 ÷ 8 = $0.70 per cup. The large bag is the better deal because $0.70 per cup is less than $0.75 per cup.

exitTicket.stem: A store sells 6 pencils for $1.50 and 10 pencils for $2.80. Which is the better buy?
choices: They cost the same per pencil
exitTicket.explanation: $1.50 ÷ 6 = $0.25 per pencil. $2.80 ÷ 10 = $0.28 per pencil. $0.25 < $0.28, so 6 for $1.50 is the better buy.
choiceFeedback: Find the unit rate for each pack, then compare them.
Calculate the cost per token for each option.
You have enough information to find and compare the rates.
hints: Better buy means the lower cost for ONE pencil — you can't compare $1.50 and $2.80 directly because the packs have different counts.
Find each pack's unit price: divide the price by the number of pencils, then compare the two per-pencil costs.
Start with the first pack: $1.50 ÷ 6 pencils. Then compute $2.80 ÷ 10 and pick the smaller per-pencil price.

watchFor.en: Listen for "Rate" — A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
watchFor.es: Escucha "Tasa" — Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.

watchFor.en: Listen for "Unit Rate" — A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
watchFor.es: Escucha "Tasa unitaria" — Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.

watchFor.en: Listen for "Per" — For each one. Example: 5 dollars per book.
watchFor.es: Escucha "Por" — Por cada uno. Ejemplo: 5 dólares por libro.

questions.stem: If 3 pounds of apples cost $6, how much do 7 pounds cost?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: $6 ÷ 3 = $2 per pound. For 7 pounds: $2 × 7 = $14.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of broth for every 10 servings. How many cups of broth are needed for 30 servings?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Multiply broth by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 cups.
Divide 6:9 by 3 to get 2:3. Since both ratios simplify to 2:3, they are equivalent.
